Danny Jones hosts a debate between a CIA spy and an FBI agent on China, Ukraine, and how states make people vanish. The episode title frames it as a spy against agent showdown. Neither man is named in the title, so the draw is the clash itself.

The two trade views on the war in Ukraine and the threat they see from China. They also talk tradecraft, the dark art of moving and hiding people across borders. Jones plays ref as each man rates the other's service. Listeners get rare shop talk from both sides of the badge. The library holds the debate as an archive record.

Physicist Hal Puthoff joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 2314. Puthoff is a rare bridge figure: a credentialed scientist who ran early remote-viewing research for the CIA and later worked on government UFO programs. His career links several of the show's favorite mysteries.

He tells Rogan what the remote-viewing trials claimed to show and how officials judged them. The talk moves on to UFO study inside government and what Puthoff thinks the data supports. Listeners get a first-hand history of America's strangest research programs, from a man who helped run them and still defends parts of the record.
podcast-tuckercarlson-Xbu0354vZp8:
Tucker Carlson charges that Americans are being poisoned while leaders look away. He points to food, water, drugs, and air as sources of harm. Sickness, in his account, has become normal and ignored.

He asks why chronic illness climbs while officials stay calm. He blames firms that profit and agencies that fail to act. The episode strings cases into a single accusation of neglect. Its tone is alarm, not balance. Listeners who feel unwell in a rich nation get a host who shares their anger and names who he holds at fault.
